Team / Evan —

Thanks for the redline, Evan. I reviewed Stellar_Health_DPA_Redline_v2.docx and prepared a short summary (attached: Redline_Summary.docx). Key points from Legal:

1) SCCs & transfer language
- We are comfortable executing the EU Commission SCCs (processor-to-controller / processor-to-processor pairings) but need to incorporate Redwoods subprocessor appendix rather than ad hoc language. Please confirm Stellars desired Appendix content (e.g., subprocessor categories vs. specific names) and whether they expect proactive notification or prior approval.

2) Liability and indemnity carveouts
- Stellar inserted a narrow carveout related to export controls. We need to negotiate tighter language; recommend negotiation call if they insist on carveout scope >$X (suggest escrow/insurance as fallback).

3) Key custody / KMS
- If Stellar requires customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key, BYOK) with Redwood never having key access, we can support a KMS integration. Laura: please confirm which cloud KMS setups we can support for a private deployment and whether HSM-backed KMS is required for their regulated flows.

4) Evidence / subprocessor list
- Procurement will want a living list of subprocessors and SOC/Security readiness evidence. We can provide SOC2 + pen test summary and a snapshot of subprocessors; for full attestation we may need a narrow NDA or an evidence binder on a shared drive.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

- KMS: Stellars security team requires HSM-backed keys and that Redwood cannot export plaintext keys. They are prepared to use a cloud KMS (customer-managed key) with role-based access controls.
- Liability carveouts: Procurement will push back on caps. They asked whether escrow/insurance proof might be an alternative.
